name: filesystem
title: Filesystem (official MCP server)
description: The official MCP filesystem server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem 2.1.0) on the folders you mount, nothing else: read_text_file (whole, head or tail), read_media_file (base64 image, audio or blob), read_multiple_files, write_file, edit_file (exact or whitespace-tolerant replacements, answered with a git-style diff; dryRun), create_directory, list_directory, list_directory_with_sizes, directory_tree (JSON), move_file, search_files (glob on names), get_file_info (size, times, permissions, hard links), list_allowed_directories. The allowed directories are exactly the folders mounted at /work and /ref1-/ref3 (an empty mount point is not allowed); MCP Roots are never used, so a client cannot widen them. Symbolic links out of them are refused, writes go through the checked directory and never through a link. No network.

mounts.description: The folder the server works on (--mount /work=FOLDER:rw to write, :ro to only read)
Another folder, best read-only (--mount /ref1=DIR:ro); a writable one is written too
Another folder, best read-only (--mount /ref2=DIR:ro); a writable one is written too
Another folder, best read-only (--mount /ref3=DIR:ro); a writable one is written too

notes: For agents on capable models that work with the reference tool set (Claude Desktop-style clients, agents written against it). For small local models the files server is the better choice: it needs the sha256 a file was read with before replacing it, reports every write and repairs Markdown; this one overwrites without asking, edits by text match and reads whole files. read-only: mount the folder :ro (every write then fails), or allow only the read tools in the client. Not stopped by the server: a write to a file that also has hard links elsewhere changes it at every name (get_file_info shows hardLinks). Version 2.3.0 (old enough from 2026-11-25) anchors reads as it anchors writes and adds read-only folders; until then a concurrent swap of a folder for a link can make a read land outside the folders, inside the container only (its image, never your files).
